headline: High-risk filesystem and git overlap: Claude Code can write the shared workspace while pdf.js can consume PDF files, creating medium prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Claude Code can write repo files and use MCP, while pdf.js reads PDF files and runs in a browser-based worker. If Claude Code places attacker-controlled content into shared files that pdf.js later processes, instruction-like content could influence downstream handling. The shared filesystem bridge is documented; no stronger parser-hijack evidence is needed.
conditions: IF Claude Code writes untrusted content into a PDF-processing input path
IF pdf.js is invoked on files produced by Claude Code without content provenance checks
mitigations: Use separate input/output directories for the two agents
Add a manual review step before pdf.js processes Claude Code outputs
Rename or quarantine generated files before opening them
Disable automatic ingestion of newly written files
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between filesystem producers and consumers

B_data_leakage.rationale: Claude Code touches source code, git history, shell environment, and files in cwd, and it has broad network egress. pdf.js touches PDF documents and has no network egress, but the shared filesystem means sensitive local files can flow from Claude Code into pdf.js outputs or screenshots/exports. The pair can therefore expose sensitive workspace data in default shared-directory setups.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same working directory
IF Claude Code reads secrets or source files that pdf.js later opens or renders
mitigations: Run each agent in a separate workspace
Keep secrets out of the shared directory
Restrict pdf.js to a read-only copy of non-sensitive PDFs
Review Claude Code outputs before saving them into shared paths
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Claude Code has write_filesystem and modify_git_state, and its concurrency model says shared state with other instances is via filesystem and git only. pdf.js can read PDF files in the same workspace. That creates a direct write/read conflict on shared mutable files and git state, with default configurations dangerous because concurrent edits can corrupt work or overwrite changes.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or directory
IF Claude Code commits or rewrites files while pdf.js is reading or generating PDFs from that workspace
mitigations: Pause one agent while the other writes
Use separate git branches per agent
Lock shared files before edits
Avoid having pdf.js write back into the repo
requires-engineering: add workspace locking or transactional file updates

D_cascading_error.rationale: Claude Code can generate or modify files and git state, while pdf.js can render or process PDFs from those files. If pdf.js treats Claude Code output as authoritative, errors can cascade from generated content into downstream documents or reviews. The pathway exists in default shared-workspace use, but pdf.js is not itself an autonomous action-taker, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF pdf.js consumes documents produced by Claude Code without verification
IF downstream reviewers rely on pdf.js-rendered output as ground truth
mitigations: Require human verification of Claude Code outputs before PDF generation
Compare rendered PDFs against source text
Keep generated documents in a staging folder
Add checksum checks before downstream use
requires-engineering: add validation gates between generation and rendering

E_compliance.rationale: Claude Code handles git credentials and shell environment data, while pdf.js only touches PDF documents and has no stated residency or retention mismatch. The main compliance concern is local handling of secrets in Claude Code, but the pair itself does not show a documented cross-border or regulated-data mismatch. I do not cite pdf.js as a compliance risk source beyond its PDF-only scope.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in the shared workspace
IF Claude Code is used on secrets that are later embedded into PDFs
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared repo
Redact secrets before PDF creation
Use separate retention policies for source and PDFs
Review logs for secret material
requires-engineering: document residency and retention boundaries
